userStories.notes:
This is the integration story that wires everything together. All tool stories (MEM-003, W01) and storage (TSK-S) must be done first. After this story, the agent has a complete memory tool suite and clean production code.

CRITICAL DESIGN INSIGHT (see docs/cua-context-management.md): The CUA agent's context is a narrow sliding window. ImageRetentionCallback keeps only the last N screenshot triplets (reasoning + computer_call + computer_call_output), and OpenAI's truncation:auto drops the rest. By turn 100, only ~20 items survive out of ~300+. This has two key implications:

1. TASK_MEMORY.md MUST be injected into the `instructions` parameter (not as a tool result), because PromptInstructionsCallback prepends it on EVERY turn — it's the only content guaranteed to never be truncated. This is the primary cross-session knowledge transfer mechanism.

2. function_call_output items (memory_search/memory_get results) are ephemeral — they get truncated by the API like everything else. The agent only benefits from search results in the turn they're retrieved. Don't rely on the agent choosing to search; the most important memory goes in instructions.

userStories.notes:
Uses the same planner model (gpt-4.1-mini) that the nudge (US-MEM-004) will eventually use when upgraded. See docs/memory-system.md for compaction design.

Two-phase compaction:
1. compact_task_memory: session-NNN.md + existing TASK_MEMORY.md → compacted TASK_MEMORY.md (task-specific)
2. compact_global_memory: compacted TASK_MEMORY.md + existing MEMORY.md → compacted MEMORY.md (cross-task patterns)

The naive append consolidation in agenthle_agent.py (post-run block, lines ~203-237) serves as the interim mechanism and becomes the fallback if LLM compaction fails. This ensures data is never lost even if the compaction model is unavailable.

WARNING — Naive append causes unbounded growth: The current post-run block appends the FULL session log verbatim to both TASK_MEMORY.md and MEMORY.md after every run. After 5+ runs, both files become bloated with redundant observations, wasting context tokens when injected into instructions. LLM compaction MUST deduplicate, compress, and resolve contradictions — not just summarize. Each compacted output should be strictly shorter than (existing content + new session log).

userStories.notes:
Pure infrastructure story — no agent behavior changes, no new tools. The agent sees the same memory_search interface; only the backend changes from O(n) file scanning to indexed FTS5 queries.

Key design decisions:
1. Markdown files remain source of truth. SQLite is a derived index that can be rebuilt from scratch.
2. The embedding_cache table is created but left empty — US-MEM-006 adds vector search on top.
3. Token estimation uses 4 chars ≈ 1 token (OpenClaw's approximation). Good enough for chunking; exact tokenization not needed.
4. SQLite DB lives at memory_data/memory.db (co-located with the markdown files it indexes).
5. No external dependencies — Python's sqlite3 module has FTS5 support built in on most platforms. If FTS5 is unavailable (rare), fall back to LIKE queries with a warning.

userStories.title: Within-session context compaction via instruction absorption
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a callback that periodically summarizes accumulated agent `message` items AND planner-written session log entries, absorbs key observations into the `instructions=` parameter, then clears old messages from context. This ensures important within-session discoveries survive OpenAI's blind truncation by being promoted to the only non-truncatable content. Also closes Gap 2 (planner→agent communication): the planner's richer observations from reasoning extraction are fed back to the agent via instructions.

userStories.notes:
This addresses Gap 1 (no within-session context compaction) AND Gap 2 (planner→agent communication) from the agent-planner architecture review (2026-03-09).

The key insight is that `instructions=` is the ONLY content guaranteed to survive all truncation — PromptInstructionsCallback prepends it on every turn. By folding important observations from both `message` items and the planner-written session log into instructions, we:
- Make within-session discoveries permanent (Gap 1)
- Feed planner observations back to the agent (Gap 2)

The planner observation flush (every 10 steps) extracts observations from reasoning summaries that the agent has already lost from context. Without this feedback loop, those observations only exist in the session log file — invisible to the agent. By including session log content as input to the compaction callback, the agent benefits from the planner's richer analysis.

Design details:
1. The callback needs a reference to the PromptInstructionsCallback instance to update its .instructions field, AND a reference to MemoryStore to read the session log. Pass both in the constructor.
2. Instructions are split into a static part (tool descriptions, task guidance) and a dynamic '## Session Observations' section. Only the dynamic section is rewritten by the planner.
3. The planner receives three inputs: (a) current ## Session Observations section, (b) agent message items from context, (c) recent session log entries. It merges all three into a compacted observation section.
4. The planner prompt must say: 'Keep the observation section under 2000 tokens. Replace older observations with newer contradicting ones. Deduplicate. Messages and session log may overlap — merge, don't duplicate.'
5. Message clearing returns a new list (not mutating in-place) to avoid aliasing issues with the agent loop's new_items.
6. on_llm_start is async in the CUA SDK — call_planner is also async, so this works naturally.

Callback ordering matters:
- PromptInstructionsCallback (prepends instructions) → ContextCompactionCallback (reads+updates instructions, filters messages) → ImageRetentionCallback (removes old screenshots) → TrajectorySaverCallback (saves final context to disk)

This ensures TrajectorySaverCallback captures the post-compaction state in api_start.json.

userStories.notes:
This addresses Gap 3 from the agent-planner architecture review (2026-03-09): planner has no memory access.

The planner is currently stateless — it only sees what callers explicitly pass in the prompt. This causes:
- Duplicate observations (planner doesn't know TASK_MEMORY.md already covers a topic)
- Missing context (planner can't search for related observations from earlier in the session)
- Weaker summaries (no task-specific background knowledge)

Design details:
1. TASK_MEMORY.md injection is automatic when store is provided — callers don't need to manually read and pass it. This is prepended to the system_prompt, not replacing it.
2. Tool definitions reuse the same parameter schemas from MemorySearchTool and MemoryGetTool (memory/tools.py) but formatted as OpenAI function calling schema.
3. Tool execution is synchronous within the async call_planner — we call store.search() and store.read_file() directly (they're sync methods on MemoryStore).
4. The max 3 rounds cap is important: the planner should quickly check memory and produce a response, not enter an exploratory search loop. If it hits the cap, return whatever content it has.
5. This is backward compatible: all existing callers that don't pass store= continue to work identically. Only callers that opt in get memory access.
6. US-MEM-COMPACT's compaction callback should also pass store when calling call_planner — but that wiring happens in US-MEM-COMPACT, not here.
